gen-gf-phudu-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Phudu opens every curve wide and draws with a plain ballpoint line. Alegreya Sans SC, a sans-serif with a gap in its c, carries a long stretch of text with a modern, welcoming ease that never tires the eye.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-almarai: Clean and a little cheeky, Phudu draws its curves with a pen-like, pressure-free line. Almarai is a plain sans whose width never swells or tapers, and its letters never pinch shut.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-amarna: Contemporary in feel, Phudu leaves generous openings at the end of every curve and keeps its line plain. Amarna, a sans-serif, runs contrast-free from stem to terminal, so even its small counters stay unclogged.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-andika: Professional but friendly, Andika, a sans-serif, gives its tails and terminals the same bulk as its stems. And Phudu leads above it with bold, wide-open curves, so a longer passage moves along with easy, rounded s turns.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-anta: Chunky, open and unmistakably loud up top. Anta follows as a sans with gaping e mouths and a wire-bent sign look, and that constant thickness is the quality the pair leans on.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-antic: Phudu's most striking trait is the generous opening at the end of every curve, drawn with a ballpoint's plain line. And Antic, a sans-serif, looks drawn with a single nib, its letter mouths left open like an unjoined chalk arc.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-ar-one-sans: Bold, pen-drawn curves lead the way, with Phudu holding a steady, unvarying line. But AR One Sans, a plain sans with lifted brush ends, would feel lost if the heading shrank or the body grew large.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-assistant: Phudu puts full-width stroke connections where thin hairline joins might be, and its curves open wide. And Assistant, a sans with mouths that stay open on c, e and a, sits quietly beneath to carry the text.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-asta-sans: Approachable from the first glance, Phudu opens its curves wide and keeps its line plain. Asta Sans, a sans with tubelike, constant-weight lines, makes its e unmistakable, and that clarity is what the pair does best.
gen-gf-phudu-gf-bai-jamjuree: Bai Jamjuree reads light and unpinched in its round letters, with no thick-and-thin shifts at all. But Phudu is the one that grabs attention with its bold, open-ended curves, while the sans simply keeps the text moving.
